# Relaxation and spin exchange {.unnumbered #relaxation-and-spin-exchange}

## Electron randomization {#electron-randomization}

Electron-randomization collisions relax electronic polarization while preserving the nuclear reduced state according to the implemented collision map. The user enters the effective rate $R_{\mathrm{ER}}$. In a coated cell this rate can represent residual wall relaxation and other electron-randomizing processes not modeled microscopically.

## Uniform ground-state relaxation {#uniform-ground-state-relaxation}

Each species has an independent rate $R_{u,a}$, with a new-session default of
$1\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$. For $N_a$ ground Zeeman states the channel is

$$
\mathcal D_{u,a}(\rho_a)=R_{u,a}
\left[\mathrm{Tr}(\rho_a)\frac{I_a}{N_a}-\rho_a\right].
$$

It conserves trace, preserves Hermiticity and positivity, and relaxes both
electronic and nuclear polarization. The target is equal population per
Zeeman state across both manifolds, so equilibrium hyperfine populations are
proportional to their degeneracies. This differs from electron randomization,
which preserves the nuclear reduced state in the collision map.

The population generator is $L_{u,a}=R_{u,a}(\mathbf1\mathbf1^T/N_a-I)$.
It enters the full population Jacobian, while every off-diagonal coherence
receives $-R_{u,a}\rho_{ij}$. Pump turn-off does not switch this channel off.
With no other dynamics, $p_i(t)=1/N_a+[p_i(0)-1/N_a]e^{-R_{u,a}t}$, and
every traceless atomic moment decays with the same exponential.

For normalized populations the signed fractional population-loss diagnostic
is $G_i^u=R_u[1-1/(N p_i)]$, undefined at zero population. Adjacent-coherence
decay is $\Gamma_i^u=R_u$. Both are included in the displayed totals and in
the linewidth used for optional RF normalization.

## Self spin exchange {#self-spin-exchange}

The self-exchange rate is calculated from the alkali density, thermal mean relative speed, and a species-specific cross section. The collision map is linearized about the calculated steady state for the RF response.

Spin exchange can transfer perturbations between coherences. It is therefore represented by a matrix contribution, not only by a scalar linewidth.

## Unlike-alkali exchange {#unlike-alkali-exchange}

When A and B are different active alkalis, the steady populations and small-signal responses are coupled. The joint coherence generator has the block form

$$
G=
\begin{pmatrix}
G_A & R_{A\leftarrow B}M_{A\leftarrow B}\\
R_{B\leftarrow A}M_{B\leftarrow A} & G_B
\end{pmatrix}.
$$

For the A response, only A is directly driven and read out, but B can influence A through the off-diagonal blocks. The B response is defined conversely.

## Relaxation reported in the app {#reported-relaxation}

The Zeeman table separates optical-pumping, electron-randomization, uniform-relaxation, self-exchange, and cross-exchange contributions. Adjacent-coherence widths enter the RF susceptibility, while population fractional rates describe redistribution of the zero-RF populations.

The numerical constants and literature sources are summarized in [References](../references.qmd).
